title: Amoebiasis and giardiasis: tissue and gut-lumen drugs
ariaLabel: Schematic of two places the amoeba lives: the tissue, where trophozoites invade the gut wall and liver, and the gut lumen, where cysts form. Metronidazole-type nitroimidazoles act on trophozoites in tissue and lumen, while luminal amoebicides such as diloxanide and paromomycin act only in the lumen.
caption: Schematic, not to scale. Flow and levels are qualitative and illustrative; no dose, concentration or lipid value is shown or implied.
blockInfo: A drug of the chosen class acting at this step (generic teaching symbol, not a named drug's shape). Less passes here, with the effects shown at the cholesterol and the LDL receptors.

nodes.label: Trophozoites in tissue
nodes.info: Invasive amoebae in the gut wall and, in liver abscess, the liver.

nodes.label: Cysts in the lumen
nodes.info: Amoebae in the gut lumen, including cysts that spread infection.

nodes.label: Luminal parasites
nodes.info: Amoebae and cysts in the lumen, the source of spread.

nodes.label: Amoebae remaining
nodes.info: A teaching score for the amoebae that remain in the body.

edges.label: nitroimidazole activation
edges.info: Metronidazole and tinidazole are activated in anaerobic organisms, where their reduced form damages DNA. They reach tissue well.
Adds to the effect shown at the right.

edges.label: luminal killing
edges.info: Luminal amoebicides (diloxanide furoate, paromomycin, iodoquinol) are not well absorbed and act in the lumen; nitroimidazoles act here too but are not enough alone to clear cysts.
Adds to the effect shown at the right.

sources: Where each class acts. Nitroimidazoles act on trophozoites in tissue, and luminal amoebicides act in the gut lumen. This is standard teaching in the pharmacology texts the PrepNucleus lessons cite (Katzung; KD Tripathi) and were not checked against a linked source here, so they are flagged for review.
simplified: Giardia, trichomonas and anaerobic bacteria, chloroquine for liver abscess, aspiration, resistance, alcohol and other adverse effects of nitroimidazoles, pregnancy and which drug suits which syndrome are left out. Amoebae remaining is drawn as a teaching score. Levels and the size of each effect are illustrative. The drug choices are teaching toggles of a class: no named drug, dose or schedule is shown or implied, and the figure does not say who should or should not take any of them.
